facts.statement: Haestasaurus was a herbivorous sauropod dinosaur belonging to the Macronaria group that lived in what is now England during the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Haestasaurus is a genus of herbivorous sauropod dinosaur, belonging to the Macronaria, that during the Early Cretaceous lived in the area of present-day England.

facts.statement: The only known species of Haestasaurus is Haestasaurus becklesii.
facts.quote: The only species is Haestasaurus becklesii.

facts.statement: Haestasaurus was a large, quadrupedal, long-necked dinosaur.
facts.quote: As a sauropod, Haestasaurus would have been a large quadrupedal long-necked dinosaur.

facts.statement: The known forelimb bones of Haestasaurus include a humerus measuring 599 millimetres, an ulna measuring 421 millimetres, and a radius measuring 404 millimetres.
facts.quote: The humerus is 599 millimetres long, the ulna 421 millimetres and the radius, situated next to the ulna in the lower arm, has a length of 404 millimetres.

facts.statement: A rock specimen associated with the forelimb, cataloged as NHMUK R1868, was the first known fossil preserving parts of sauropod skin.
facts.quote: A rock associated with the forelimb, NHMUK R1868, was the first specimen known preserving parts of the sauropod skin.

facts.statement: A 2022 study identified small protuberances or papillae on the scales of Haestasaurus.
facts.quote: In 2022 a study reported the presence of small covering protuberances or papillae on the scales.

facts.statement: The fossil material was collected in 1852 by Samuel Husband Beckles from Wealden Sandstone exposed at low tide near Hastings, East Sussex.
facts.quote: In 1852, the collector Samuel Husband Beckles obtained a block of Wealden Sandstone that had become visible at low tide off the coast of East Sussex near Hastings.

facts.statement: The precise location where the fossils were found is now unknown.
facts.quote: The precise location is today unknown.

facts.statement: Paul Upchurch, Philip D. Mannion, and Michael P. Taylor established the separate genus Haestasaurus in 2015 after determining it was distinct from Pelorosaurus conybeari.
facts.quote: In 2015, Paul Upchurch, Philip D. Mannion and Michael P. Taylor, having established that P. becklesii differed in many traits from Pelorosaurus conybeari and was not its sister species, named the separate genus Haestasaurus.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen dates to the Berriasian-Valanginian stages of the Early Cretaceous, approximately 140 million years ago.
facts.quote: The holotype, NHMUK R1870, was found in a layer of the Hastings Beds dating from the Berriasian-Valanginian, roughly 140 million years old.

facts.statement: Researchers favor the classification of Haestasaurus as a rare, late-surviving basal member of the Macronaria clade.
facts.quote: Haestasaurus would then represent a rare late-surviving basal macronarian.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Haestasaurus belongs to the Titanosauria or is a basal Macronarian, as limited fossil material prevents a single definitive solution.
facts.quote: Due to the limited material available however, it proved impossible to obtain a single solution to this problem.

facts.statement: The skin scales of Haestasaurus gradually decreased in size, possibly toward the elbow, to allow for greater flexibility.
facts.quote: The scales gradually decrease in size, perhaps towards the elbow, to provide it greater flexibility.

facts.statement: Haestasaurus was a large, long-necked, four-legged herbivorous sauropod.
facts.quote: Siendo un saurópodo, Haestasaurus era un gran herbívoro cuadrúpedo de cuello alargado.

facts.statement: The known forelimb bones include a humerus measuring 599 mm, a cubit measuring 421 mm, and a radius measuring 404 mm.
facts.quote: El húmero mide 599 milímetros de largo, el cúbito es de 421 milímetros y el radio, situado junto al cúbito en el antebrazo, tiene una longitud de 404 milímetros.

facts.statement: A rock associated with the forelimb, specimen NHMUK R1868, was the first known sauropod specimen to preserve skin parts.
facts.quote: Una roca asociada con la extremidad delantera, NHMUK R1868, fue el primer espécimen conocido que preservaba partes de piel de saurópodo.

facts.statement: Collector Samuel Husband Beckles obtained a rock block from the Wealden Sandstone near Hastings, East Sussex, in 1852.
facts.quote: En 1852, el coleccionista Samuel Husband Beckles obtuvo un bloque de roca de la Arenisca de Wealden que se había hecho visible durante una marea baja en la costa de East Sussex cerca de Hastings.

facts.statement: Paul Upchurch, Philip D. Mannion, and Michael P. Taylor established the independent genus Haestasaurus in 2015 after finding it distinct from Pelorosaurus conybeari.
facts.quote: En 2015, Paul Upchurch, Philip D. Mannion y Michael P. Taylor, habiendo establecido que P. becklesii difería en muchos rasgos de Pelorosaurus conybeari y que no era su especie hermana, nombraron al género independiente Haestasaurus.

facts.statement: The genus name Haestasaurus is derived from the Saxon tribal leader Haesta and the Greek word sauros meaning reptile.
facts.quote: El nombre del género se deriva de Haesta, el presunto jefe tribal sajón del . cuya existencia se ha deducido del nombre original de Hastings, Haestingas, "el pueblo de Haesta", y el término griego sauros, "reptil".

facts.statement: The holotype was found in the Hastings Beds dating to the Berriasian to Valanginian stages, approximately 140 million years ago.
facts.quote: El holotipo, NHMUK R1870, fue hallado en una capa de los Lechos de Hastings que data de las épocas del Berriasiense al Valanginiense, hace aproximadamente 140 millones de años.

facts.statement: Haestasaurus lived between 139.1 and 132.6 million years ago during the Berriasian to Valanginian periods.
facts.quote: Time range: Berriasian to Valanginian (139.1 to 132.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Haestasaurus may represent the late survival of a rare basal macronarian.
facts.quote: Haestasaurus podría representar la supervivencia tardía de un raro macronariano basal.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Haestasaurus was a basal member of Titanosauria or a basal Macronarian closely related to dinosaurs like Camarasaurus.
facts.quote: Una posibilidad sería que Haestasaurus fue en realidad un miembro basal de Titanosauria. La otra idea es que en cambio Haestasaurus fuese un miembro basal de un clado mayor, los Macronaria, y por lo tanto fuera un pariente cercano de dinosaurios como Camarasaurus, Janenschia o Tehuelchesaurus.

facts.statement: The preserved area of the skin impression measures 215 mm by 195 mm.
facts.quote: El área preservada es de 215 milímetros por 195 mm.
